intro: Thai people are warm already, but say a word or two in Thai and the smiles get bigger. These are the most useful phrases in easy romanized pronunciation — a little effort goes a long way.

blocks.html: Start here: the two phrases you will use most are "hello" and "thank you". The key to polite Thai is the ending particle — men add "khrap", women add "kha" to the end of a sentence, and it instantly sounds more polite.

blocks.title: Don’t worry about perfect tones
blocks.html: Thai is tonal, so tones can change meaning — but most Thais understand from context and appreciate the effort. Smile and give it a go; locals love it when you try.

faq.q: How do you say hello in Thai?
faq.a: Say "sà-wàt-dii" and add the polite particle — "khráp" if you are male, "khâ" if you are female. It works for both hello and goodbye.

faq.q: How do you say thank you in Thai?
faq.a: Say "khàwp-khun" followed by "khráp" (male) or "khâ" (female) to sound polite.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Thai to travel here?
faq.a: Not at all — basic English gets by in tourist areas. But knowing 5–10 basic words makes the trip more fun and delights locals.

quickAnswerHtml: Start with hello and thank you, then add the polite ending — "khrap" for men, "kha" for women — and you instantly sound respectful. Thai people understand from context and love that you tried; perfect tones aren't required to connect.
